instruction: Set the title alignment to center for slides 1 through 3.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires center-aligning titles in slides 1, 2, and 3 (0-indexed as 0, 1, 2). Evaluator extracts paragraph alignment from title shapes and checks if it equals PP_ALIGN.CENTER (value 2). Partial credit given for each correctly aligned slide (1/3 per slide).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: center-aligning titles in slides 1, 2, and 3
Getter logic is sound: retrieves file, opens PowerPoint, extracts title alignment from specified slides (0-indexed as 0, 1, 2)
Metric logic is correct: compares actual alignment vs expected CENTER (value 2), provides appropriate partial credit (1/3 per slide)
Data flow is correct: postconfig saves file, getter retrieves saved file, alignment values are properly extracted and compared
Expected values are semantically correct: slides [0, 1, 2] maps to slides 1-3, alignment value 2 equals PP_ALIGN.CENTER
Edge cases handled: missing slides, missing title shapes (fallback to first text shape), None alignment (converts to LEFT)
Complete instruction coverage: all three slides are checked for center alignment
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor consideration: The fallback to 'first text shape with content' when no formal title shape exists is pragmatic but could theoretically select wrong shape on unusual slide layouts. This is acceptable given real-world PowerPoint usage patterns.
